objects.definition: typedef uint tchar;         /* single, full character */
objects.description: Project-defined character code unit represented as an unsigned int (via uint). Intended to hold a full character code; exact width/platform semantics depend on uint.

objects.definition: typedef char tmbchar;       /* single, possibly partial character */
objects.description: Project-defined narrow character unit (possibly part of a multi-byte sequence).

objects.definition:
typedef tmbchar* tmbstr;    /* pointer to buffer of possibly partial chars */
typedef const tmbchar* ctmbstr; /* Ditto, but const */
objects.description: Pointer typedefs for buffers of tmbchar. tmbstr is mutable, ctmbstr is a const pointer to such data. Alias relationship noted via aliases list using pointer-name convention as required.
Project-specific boolean enum with values no (0) and yes (1). Useful where C89 compatibility or reserved word conflicts with C++ bool are a concern.

objects.definition:
struct _TidyIterator { int _opaque; };
typedef struct _TidyIterator const * TidyIterator;
objects.description: Opaque iterator handle for traversing collections. It is a pointer to a const opaque struct and should be treated as an abstract token; contents are not to be accessed by users. Note the typedef is to a const-pointer type; users pass and store TidyIterator by value (which is already a pointer).

objects.definition: TIDY_STRUCT struct _TidyBuffer;

Growable byte buffer used by HTML Tidy for I/O. Tracks allocator, data pointer, current size in use, total allocated bytes, and the next read position (for input semantics). The public API provides initialization, allocation/reallocation, attach/detach to external memory, clear/free, and byte/array push/pop/get/unget, plus adapters to use it as input or output sources. functions.name: tidyBufInit
functions.signature: void tidyBufInit(TidyBuffer* buf);
functions.description: Initialize a TidyBuffer using the default allocator. Sets fields to a valid, empty state so it can be used for subsequent allocations and I/O operations.
requirements: buf must be a valid, non-null pointer to a TidyBuffer.
May be called on an uninitialized TidyBuffer before any other tidyBuf* operations.
Do not assume any existing content in buf is preserved; this prepares an empty buffer.

functions.name: tidyBufInitWithAllocator
functions.signature: void tidyBufInitWithAllocator(TidyBuffer* buf, TidyAllocator* allocator);
functions.description: Initialize a TidyBuffer using a caller-provided custom allocator. Prepares the buffer for use with the given allocator.
requirements: buf must be a valid, non-null pointer to a TidyBuffer.
allocator must be a valid, non-null pointer to a TidyAllocator that remains valid for the lifetime of the buffer.
Should be called before any other operations on buf.

functions.name: tidyBufAlloc
functions.signature: void tidyBufAlloc(TidyBuffer* buf, uint allocSize);
functions.description: Free any current contents of the buffer, allocate the given capacity using the default allocator, and reset the input (read) pointer. Results in an empty buffer with at least allocSize capacity.
requirements: buf must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized TidyBuffer (initialized via tidyBufInit or equivalent).
allocSize is the capacity to allocate in bytes; must be a valid size representable by uint.
Existing buffer contents will be freed; callers must not rely on previous pointers into the buffer after this call.

functions.name: tidyBufAllocWithAllocator
functions.signature: void tidyBufAllocWithAllocator(TidyBuffer* buf, TidyAllocator* allocator, uint allocSize);
functions.description: Free any current contents, allocate the given capacity with a provided custom allocator, and reset the input (read) pointer. Uses the specified allocator for the buffer.
requirements: buf must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized TidyBuffer or a TidyBuffer owned by the caller.
allocator must be a valid, non-null TidyAllocator pointer and must remain valid for the lifetime of the buffer.
allocSize is the capacity to allocate in bytes; must fit in uint.
Existing contents are freed and invalidated.

functions.name: tidyBufCheckAlloc
functions.signature: void tidyBufCheckAlloc(TidyBuffer* buf, uint allocSize, uint chunkSize);
functions.description: Ensure the buffer is expanded to at least allocSize bytes of capacity. If growth is needed, the buffer grows in chunks (minimum growth is chunkSize). Passing 0 uses a default chunk size of 256 bytes.
requirements: buf must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized TidyBuffer.
allocSize specifies the minimum capacity required; must be representable in uint.
chunkSize may be 0 to request the default growth size; otherwise it specifies the minimum growth chunk size in bytes.

functions.name: tidyBufFree
functions.signature: void tidyBufFree(TidyBuffer* buf);
functions.description: Free the buffer’s current contents and reset its state to zeroed/empty. After this call the buffer holds no data.
requirements: buf must be a valid, non-null pointer to a TidyBuffer (initialized or previously used).
After freeing, any previously obtained pointers into the buffer become invalid.
Safe to call when you want to release memory associated with the buffer’s contents.

functions.name: tidyBufClear
functions.signature: void tidyBufClear(TidyBuffer* buf);
functions.description: Set all buffer bytes to 0. Does not change allocation, but clears the contents to zero.
requirements: buf must be a valid, non-null pointer to an initialized TidyBuffer.
The buffer must have allocated storage; otherwise clearing has no effect or is a no-op (exact behavior not documented).
Caller should not assume size is changed unless implementation explicitly sets size to 0; header only states bytes are set to 0 (details unknown).

functions.name: tidyBufAttach
functions.signature: void tidyBufAttach(TidyBuffer* buf, byte* bp, uint size);
functions.description: Attach the TidyBuffer to an existing caller-provided memory region. The buffer will reference the provided memory without allocating its own.
requirements: buf must be a valid, non-null pointer to a TidyBuffer.
bp must point to a valid memory block of at least size bytes that remains valid for the duration of the attachment.
size must reflect the number of bytes available at bp.

        count = rng.randint(1, 4)
        items = rng.sample(MUTE_KEYS, k=min(count, len(MUTE_KEYS)))

    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4)):

# Our generator should emit bytes that represent a plausible path string.
# Goals:
# - Generate a mixture of absolute/relative paths.
# - Include directories that likely exist (/tmp, /var/tmp, C:\\Windows\\Temp, . , ..).
# - Include writable temp-like paths for save operations.
# - Include paths with extensions (.html, .cfg, .txt) relevant to LibTidy usage.
# - Include special characters, spaces, unicode, and long components but keep under 4096 bytes.
# - Seeded randomness.

_POSIX_SEP = "/"

# Common base directories per platform semantics; the fuzzer environment may be Linux-like.
COMMON_BASES_POSIX = [
    ".",
    "..",
    "/tmp",
    "/var/tmp",
    "/dev/shm",

]

COMMON_BASES_WIN = [

]

    "report.txt",

]

    "data",
    "🧪tests",
    "..",
    ".",
    "assets",
    "css",
    "js",
    "深い",
]

EXTS = [".html", ".htm", ".xhtml", ".cfg", ".txt", ".log", ""]

# Characters safe for filenames plus some unicode
SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_ ."
UNICODE_SAMPLES = ["α", "β", "ç", "ñ", "漢", "字", "🙂", "Ω"]


def _rand_component(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12) -> str:
    # Occasionally use a predefined interesting component
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        return r.choice(EXTRA_COMPONENTS)
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(n)).strip()
    # ensure not empty after strip
    if not s:
        s = "x"
    # sprinkle unicode sometimes
    if r.random() < 0.3:
        s += r.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
    return s


def _maybe_ext(r: random.Random) -> str:
    return r.choice(EXTS)


def _rand_basename(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        base = r.choice(BASENAMES)
    else:
        base = ''.join(r.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 10))).strip()
        if not base:
            base = "file"
        base += _maybe_ext(r)
    # Occasionally ensure .cfg for tidyOptSaveFile relevance
    if r.random() < 0.15:
        if not base.endswith(".cfg"):
            base += ".cfg"
    return base


def _build_posix_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = r.choice(COMMON_BASES_POSIX)
    components: List[str] = []
    # Depth 0-5
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 5)):
        components.append(_rand_component(r))
    leaf = _rand_basename(r)
    parts = [base] + components + [leaf]
    path = _POSIX_SEP.join(parts)
    # Normalize multiple slashes lightly
    while "//" in path:
        path = path.replace("//", "/")
    return path


def _build_windows_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    base = r.choice(COMMON_BASES_WIN)
    components: List[str] = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(0, 4)):
        c = _rand_component(r)
        # Avoid path-breaking characters for Windows components
        c = c.replace("/", "-")
        c = c.replace("\\", "-")
        components.append(c)
    leaf = _rand_basename(r)
    parts = [base] + components + [leaf]
    # Ensure correct separator joining
    path = parts[0]
    for p in parts[1:]:
        if not path.endswith(_WINDOWS_SEP):
            path += _WINDOWS_SEP
        path += p
    return path

    # Specific interesting paths to hit behaviors in stubs
    cases = [
        "./out/out.html",
        "./cfg/tidy.cfg",
        "/tmp/tidy-out.html",
        "/tmp/tidy-errors.log",
        "index.html",
        "./index.html",
        "../input.html",
    ]
    # Add some with spaces and unicode
    cases += [
        "/tmp/my page.html",
        "/var/tmp/报告.xhtml",
    ]
    return cases


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a strategy
    strat = r.random()
    if strat < 0.2:
        path = r.choice(_special_cases(r))
    elif strat < 0.7:
        path = _build_posix_path(r)
    else:
        path = _build_windows_path(r)

    # Ensure the path length and encoding constraints
    # Keep under 4096 bytes; truncate if necessary at a boundary
    b = path.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    if len(b) > 4000:
        b = b[:4000]
        # Avoid cutting multi-byte character mid-way; re-decode and re-encode safely
        try:
            path = b.decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
            b = path.encode("utf-8")
        except Exception:
            pass

    return b
